hh_keeper.text: Eight hundred years, that tower. I'm only in it forty. But the stairs know me.
When the monks kept it, they burned a fire on the top. It's brighter now. It's also easier on the arms.

hh_greenway.text: I'm doing the Waterford Greenway. Forty-six kilometres, flat the whole way, and a tunnel with the lights on. I've never been happier.
It used to be a railway, and there was no bike in the whole thing. Now there are only bikes. It's a better arrangement.

hh_fisher.text: The Saltees are out there, a few miles. A Wexford man bought one in 1943 and crowned himself prince. Nobody argued. It was cheaper than an argument.
Gannets, puffins, seals. The islands are the best birdwatching in the south-east. And the prince's throne is still out there, a chair on a rock.
